description: We are a group of enthusistic physics aproching some new horizons.
summary: SPHEREx Blink is a web tool that turns NASA's SPHEREx all-sky infrared images into a blink comparator. You type a name or sky coordinates and it shows the same patch of sky at each SPHEREx visit as a short animation, with a difference image, so anything that moved or changed stands out. It addresses the challenge by making this possible for anyone, with no astronomy software. Because the archive's search service was offline during the hackathon, we built our own index of about 270,000 exposures from the public cloud copy of the data and make our own image cutouts. We ran all five test targets on real data. We measured the motion of Barnard's Star over one year (10.2 arcseconds, in agreement with the catalog) and of the brown dwarf pair Epsilon Indi B. This matters because SPHEREx images over a billion objects and nearby objects reveal themselves by moving; the public can help find them.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Enter a name or RA/Dec and SPHEREx Blink finds every SPHEREx exposure covering that position, builds one image per visit, and plays them as a blink animation. It also shows a difference image, a sum image, a comparison within a single detector band, an adjustable field of view, and coordinates in the URL so a view can be shared or embedded. It measures the position of the central source in every exposure and reports the shift between visits with error bars.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Sky index: we read the pointing of about 270,000 exposures from the public SPHEREx bucket once; any coordinate is then matched in milliseconds.

2. Cutouts: HTTP byte-range requests fetch only the image rows needed instead of each 71 MB file.

3. A priority queue interleaves visits and detectors so every visit gets frames early.

4. Exposures are reprojected with the full distortion model and combined per visit and per detector.

5. A profile fit on each exposure gives positions; saturated pixels are excluded.

RESULTS ON REAL DATA

Barnard's Star (Aug 2025 to Aug 2026): measured -0.98" +/- 0.10 east-west and +10.17" +/- 0.10 north-south; catalog -0.77" and +10.25".

Epsilon Indi B (1.4 years): measured +4.77" +/- 0.36 and -4.19" +/- 0.41; catalog +5.24" and -3.87".

RW Aurigae and R Draconis saturate the detector. WISE 0855 was too faint to detect in single exposures.

LIMITATIONS

Error bars are statistical only. Saturated stars show a bias of about 1.5" between visits six months apart. Spectra are not validated. Gaia overlay is not implemented. The public demo serves the five test targets; other coordinates require running the tool locally.

TOOLS

Python, Astropy, SciPy, reproject, FastAPI, Matplotlib, HTML/JavaScript, Docker.
